main_text.p: de prædestinatione, de Antichristo, de novissimis temporibus &c. contineri, quare in firmam esse vim argumenti. Fateor Veteres de obscuritate Epistolę ad Roma-mos[?] aliquando conquestos. Fusius Orige-nes initio Commentariorum in Epistolā. Alij de perplexitate Epistolæ ad Ephe-sios. Unde Epistola illa Ambrosÿ ad Ire-næum, quæ est xxxvii. Lib.v.Epist. At verò 1. non negamus esse etiam alibi quædam obscura & perplexa, ad quæ Petrus pariter respexerit; sed negamus eò respexisse exclusivè ad Epistolam ad Hebræos, vel respexisse principaliter, quod falsum esse probavimus suprà. II. Supponitur gratis, imò pernegatur eundem esse difficultatis gradum & modum in Paulinarum ullá, qui in Epistolá ad Hebræos; imò verò hujus nonnulla, comparatè præ cæteris, sunt quædam quasi Sibyllæ folia, & sacræ Sphyngis ænigmata, eminenter [illegible, ~6 letters], quanquàm nec simpliciter, nec suâ naturâ talia, nec æqualiter omnibus, pro gradu luminis & mensurâ gratiæ. Deniq; si quis nolit necessaria esse & apodictica hæc argumenta, per nos sane licuerit. Hactenus metam

page.notes: The word after "eminenter" is a Greek word in a mixed Greek/Latin printed form and is not legible at this scan resolution. "Roma-mos" is hyphenated across the line end; the second part is uncertain. The "1." before "non negamus" is kept as printed. Scan is of a sharp but aged print with some blotting in the margins, which I did not transcribe.
